subject.title: Validate required run artifacts against a schema (`--require-artifact-schema`)

question: Should Crabbox own a built-in, intentionally limited JSON artifact-schema gate, or should artifact content validation remain the responsibility of each repository's run command?
rationale: Both directions are technically viable, but choosing one establishes a durable CLI and schema-language contract that cannot be inferred from current code because the documentation currently assigns validation to repository commands.

options.title: Adopt the bounded core gate
options.body: Approve the fail-closed schema subset as a generic Crabbox evidence feature, subject to compatibility review and real SSH-backed proof on https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/1071.

options.title: Keep validation repository-owned
options.body: Retain the current existence-only gate and require repositories to validate their own evidence formats within the executed command.

options.title: Require a standard validator
options.body: Approve the capability only if the implementation uses a recognized JSON Schema contract rather than creating a Crabbox-specific subset.

recommendation.title: Adopt the bounded core gate
recommendation.body: Approve the fail-closed schema subset as a generic Crabbox evidence feature, subject to compatibility review and real SSH-backed proof on https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/1071.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to the central CLI and provider contracts affected by the product-boundary decision.
